name: Pelican
label: Hydra Head
lede: Four Chicagoans kept metal's riffs and left the singer out. Their songs ran so long that a 75-minute set held five of them, and the second guitar chair changed hands twice.

eras.title: Out of the grind
eras.text: Trevor de Brauw and drummer Larry Herweg came out of Tusk, an experimental grind band from Chicago's heavy underground. They added a second guitarist, Laurent Schroeder-Lebec, and Larry's brother Bryan on bass, skipped the vocalist, and landed on Hydra Head, the label run by Isis's Aaron Turner.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pelican · Run For Cover Records
yt: Full set, Underground Lounge, Chicago, October 2002
years.h: Pelican starts without a singer because none of them could make one fit
years.p: Trevor de Brauw and Laurent Schroeder-Lebec play guitar, brothers Bryan and Larry Herweg play bass and drums, and nobody sings.
years.xp:
De Brauw and Larry Herweg came from Tusk, an experimental grind project with their friend Jody Minnoch. De Brauw has said Pelican isn't instrumental by design: "We just didn't know how to put vocals in our music and for it to sound right."

Bryan Herweg has a theory about why nobody can file them: "If we had some big burly man in front screaming, we'd be classified as metal. If we had some scrawny guy we'd be emo." Pelican's own label bio lists influences from post-hardcore and space rock to emo and metal.

years.h: Sanford Parker records the first Pelican EP
years.p: The self-titled EP is Pelican's first release, on Hydra Head. Parker, a Chicago engineer, would record the band again 22 years later.

yt: Australasia, live at the Abbey Pub, Chicago, June 2003
years.h: Australasia is made fast, on a small budget, in a studio still being built
years.p: Pelican records its debut album at Volume Studios in Chicago with Sanford Parker. Trevor de Brauw says the budget forced the rush and the construction crew didn't help.
years.xp:
Six songs, 50 minutes and 18 seconds. NightEndDay runs 11:15, Angel Tears 10:59, the title track 10:49, Drought 8:24. De Brauw said the sessions were rushed "because of budget restrictions" and that the studio was under construction during recording.

Drought turned up in the 2009 war film The Messenger. The Abbey Pub video is from June 11, 2003, months before the record came out.

eras.title: Heavy without a word
eras.text: Touring hard in Europe and the US, Pelican became the name writers reached for once they started saying post-metal. The records grew more melodic and were cut at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio. Some early fans missed the sludge; the metal press took the band seriously anyway.

years.cap: Pelican at Sant Feliu Fest, Spain, 2004
years.h: A year after Australasia, Pelican plays a festival in Catalonia
years.p: Sant Feliu Fest in 2004 is one of the first European festivals on the band's schedule.

years.big: "The original title was going to be Black Doom on Tuesday."
q: The title is meant to confuse people.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Fire in Our Throats
years.h: Acoustic guitar arrives on The Fire in Our Throats Will Beckon the Thaw
years.p: Recorded in February 2005 at Electrical Audio with more time and a better room than Australasia got. Nature themes run through Aurora Borealis; Decibel named it the best album of 2005.
years.xp:
The album moved from Australasia's crush toward layered melody, and some longtime fans didn't love it. Critics reached for doom metal, post-rock and [[Isis|5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265]]. It reached No. 44 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart, and Terrorizer put it at No. 35 for the year.

Scott Alisoglu of Blabbermouth wrote that it is "a heavy rock album. The band just paints with more colors and uses a bigger canvas on this one."
play: The Fire in Our Throats Will Beckon the Thaw

years.h: Andrew Schneider produces Pelican's third album at Electrical Audio
years.p: On December 13, 2006, Pelican records what becomes City of Echoes at Steve Albini's studio in Chicago.

years.h: Laurent Schroeder-Lebec calls City of Echoes the pop album
years.p: Shorter songs, bigger melodies. The old ones were so long that Pelican could play five of them in a 75-minute set.
years.xp:
Schroeder-Lebec explained the math: "Even if we had a 75-minute-long set, we could only play five songs." Trevor de Brauw said the title was about globalization: you go to a lot of different places and see how much they look alike. The band said it wasn't all gloom, since touring was how they met audiences worldwide.

Pitchfork gave it 4.4; Decibel ranked it No. 13 of 2007. It reached No. 9 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and No. 40 on Independent Albums, and Dead Between the Walls in May 2008 became the band's first music video.

eras.title: Overextended
eras.text: Pelican moved from Hydra Head to Southern Lord, got its biggest recording budget, and put a vocal on a record for the first time. It also wore itself down: too much touring, illness in the family, and a founding guitarist who had stopped coming on the road.

years.h: Pelican leaves Hydra Head for Greg Anderson's Southern Lord
years.p: Southern Lord is run by [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]]'s [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]], who ends up on Pelican's next album.

years.h: Ephemeral EP goes on the road with Wolves in the Throne Room
years.p: It's Pelican's first Southern Lord release, and the tour with [[Wolves in the Throne Room|e9452446-7702-4853-96ce-5dfe6748d3fb]] supports it. The title song later plays over the end credits of Dead Space 3.

years.src: Wikipedia: What We All Come to Need · Wikipedia: Pelican
years.h: Pelican gets a singer for one song
years.p: [[Allen Epley|7b7fb455-c63c-49ca-82f4-b9c8da828bf0]] of [[Shiner|85e4c862-bafe-48a2-a7af-b87cc3d8a7f3]] sings the closer Final Breath on What We All Come to Need, Pelican's first vocal on a studio album. [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]] and [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] also guest.
years.xp:
It was recorded in July 2009, three weeks across Robert Lang Studios in Shoreline and Red Room Studio in Seattle, with Chris Common. Bryan Herweg wrote Final Breath with a vocalist in mind from the start.

Chicago's Kuma's Corner served a one-night-only Pelican burger, Kobe beef and scallops. Trevor de Brauw and Laurent Schroeder-Lebec are both vegan and couldn't eat it.

The band was worn down. De Brauw's mother was seriously ill, and he said later: "By the end of the year we had way overextended ourselves." Critics split: Metacritic 79, Pitchfork 5.5 out of 10.
play: What We All Come to Need

years.h: Roadburn and Dunk anchor Pelican's spring 2012 tour of Europe
years.p: The dates in the Netherlands and Belgium come with Bo Ningen, Tacoma Narrows Bridge Disaster and Tombs in support.

years.h: Laurent Schroeder-Lebec, off the road since 2010, leaves Pelican
years.p: He quits after the Ataraxia/Taraxis EP, telling the band his heart wasn't fully in it. Dallas Thomas of The Swan King, who had been filling in on tour, becomes a full member.
years.xp:
Thomas had played live but not written. Now he became a songwriter too, and the next record would be the first without a founder.

De Brauw described the new dynamic this way: he and Bryan Herweg are "more freewheeling", while Thomas "is very meticulous."

eras.title: Darker, and grieving
eras.text: With Dallas Thomas on guitar, Pelican got angrier. Then Jody Minnoch, an old friend from the Tusk days, died, and de Brauw and Herweg went back to their grind roots for the band's first album on a UK chart.

years.cap: Pelican in the studio during the Dallas Thomas years
years.h: Forever Becoming arrives angry, and without a founder
years.p: Recorded at Electrical Audio with Chris Common, it is, de Brauw said, "a lot darker, depressive, and angry" because of the nervous headspace after Schroeder-Lebec's exit. No. 21 on Billboard's Top Hard Rock Albums.
years.xp:
Metacritic scored it 74. The A.V. Club gave it an A-minus and Consequence of Sound a C-plus. It also reached No. 7 on Heatseekers.

A 2019 reissue was remixed and remastered at Chris Common's studio, because the original had been made in less than ideal circumstances.

years.cap: Pelican around the release of Nighttime Stories, 2019
years.h: Nighttime Stories is written for Jody Minnoch
years.p: Jody Minnoch, Trevor de Brauw and Larry Herweg's bandmate in Tusk, died suddenly of an undiagnosed heart condition. The album's title was meant for a future Tusk record.
years.xp:
De Brauw and Herweg went back to Tusk's grind for fuel, and de Brauw called the chord voicings discordant and menacing, more negative than Pelican had sounded. It was recorded at Electrical Audio and Decade Music Studios, mixed by Matt Bayles, with artwork by [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]].

Metacritic scored it 82. It reached No. 37 on the UK Rock & Metal chart, Pelican's first chart album in Britain. NPR called Midnight and Mescaline a barrage of heavy riffs. De Brauw on his guitar: "I've been playing the same 1972 Gibson SG since day one in this band."

years.h: Cloakroom and Slow Crush share the Nighttime Stories tour
years.p: Pelican plays the US, Canada, the UK and mainland Europe, with [[Cloakroom|d419f6da-298a-40ea-ba0c-1757edd218b7]] on the US dates and Slow Crush in the UK.

eras.title: Laurent comes home
eras.text: Dallas Thomas left, Laurent Schroeder-Lebec came back, and the original four were together again. The early records got deluxe reissues, and a new label, Run for Cover Records, put out Pelican's first album in six years.

years.h: Laurent Schroeder-Lebec comes back, and the original four play together again
years.p: With Dallas Thomas gone, the founding guitarist rejoins Pelican for live shows.

years.h: Pelican's first three albums get deluxe remasters
years.p: Wikipedia lists Australasia, The Fire in Our Throats Will Beckon the Thaw and City of Echoes as reissued through Thrill Jockey.

years.cap: Pelican against the Chicago skyline, around 2025
years.h: Cascading Crescent ends six years without a new Pelican song
years.p: Released February 12, it is the first single from Pelican's seventh album. Indelible follows March 18, Pining For Ever April 22 and Gulch May 13.

years.src: Wikipedia: Flickering Resonance · Run For Cover Records
years.h: The original four make Flickering Resonance with Sanford Parker again
years.p: Recorded at Chicago's Narwhal Studios by Parker, who made their first EP, it is Laurent Schroeder-Lebec's first Pelican studio album since 2009. Pelican tours it with [[Russian Circles|cca40a67-e959-46f8-a3f3-8a3f77d2da9e]].
years.xp:
Run for Cover describes a more collaborative record, with all four sharing decisions. Eight tracks, 51 minutes, opening with the 2:47 Gulch. Christian Degn's cover centers on a flame, about how the smallest flames can bring the biggest changes.

The tour ran through 2025 across North America and Europe: Russian Circles in March, Porcelain in July.
